title: Playwright MCP
claims: Playwright MCP exposes browser control through structured accessibility snapshots.
The documented server supports multiple browser engines and capability-gated tool groups.
notes: Package/runtime behavior remains untested locally; adoption needs an exact version pin.

title: Playwright MCP capabilities
claims: Core tools are enabled by default and other tool groups are opt-in.
Documented groups include storage, testing, developer tools, PDF, vision and network.
notes: Capability exposure is not a Splyce authorization decision.

title: Playwright MCP configuration
claims: Documentation describes headed/headless modes, browser choice, device emulation and shared browser context options.
Configuration includes options that broaden file-access scope.
notes: Use a dedicated profile and explicit policy for every expanded authority.

title: Connecting to browsers
claims: Playwright MCP can connect to an already-running Chromium-based browser through documented mechanisms.
notes: An existing authenticated browser is delegated authority and requires separate qualification.

title: Get started with Chrome DevTools for agents
claims: Chrome DevTools for agents exposes Chrome control and inspection through MCP.
Its documentation warns that an agent can access and act through data available in an authenticated browser session.
notes: Chrome-specific candidate; no local session was connected.

title: WebDriver BiDi
claims: WebDriver BiDi specifies bidirectional remote browser automation messages.
notes: Target browser support and feature negotiation require runtime qualification.

title: browser-use documentation
claims: browser-use documents an agent-oriented browser-control library and browser/profile configuration.
notes: Candidate only; verify profile and data handling before integration.

title: Stagehand documentation
claims: Stagehand documents browser automation and extraction APIs.
notes: Candidate only; pin source and compare on controlled fixtures.

title: UI Automation
claims: Windows UI Automation provides programmatic access to desktop UI elements for accessibility and automated testing.
notes: Application provider coverage still determines which controls are available.

title: Apple Accessibility
claims: Apple documents accessibility APIs and accessibility elements for its platforms.
notes: Consent and target-app coverage need native qualification.

title: AT-SPI2 Core API reference
claims: AT-SPI2 documents accessibility objects, roles and interfaces for desktop applications.
notes: Linux desktop and toolkit coverage is variable.

title: XDG Desktop Portal documentation
claims: XDG Desktop Portal documents desktop services exposed through a portal interface.
notes: Backend availability and semantics need session-specific tests.

title: Android Debug Bridge
claims: ADB is a command-line tool for communicating with Android devices and emulators.
notes: Device authorization and disconnection handling remain qualification work.

title: XCTest user interface tests
claims: Apple documents XCTest user interface tests for interacting with an app's UI.
notes: Apple toolchain and device/provisioning constraints need a real fixture.

title: Appium documentation
claims: Appium documents a driver-based automation ecosystem for mobile and other platforms.
notes: Driver, platform and server versions must be pinned together.

title: MCP authorization specification
claims: The MCP HTTP authorization specification documents issuer validation and resource-oriented authorization guidance.
notes: Transport authorization is distinct from local per-effect policy.

title: OAuth 2.0 for Native Apps
claims: RFC 8252 profiles OAuth 2.0 use by native applications and discusses public-client protections.
notes: Credential issuance does not grant arbitrary tool or resource access.

title: MediaDevices.getDisplayMedia
claims: Screen capture requires user selection/permission and transient user activation.
Permission to capture cannot be persisted for reuse.
notes: Browser permission is not a Splyce approval receipt.

title: Clipboard API
claims: The Clipboard API provides programmatic clipboard read/write facilities subject to browser security requirements.
notes: Treat clipboard content as sensitive private artifact data.

title: File System API
claims: Web file-system access beyond origin-private storage is subject to user consent.
notes: Local file access must be separately scoped and retained as a private artifact.
